new.title: See the Venetian Famagusta Gate
new.desc: The eastern gate of Nicosia's 1567 Venetian walls, designed by Giulio Savorgnano, was originally called Porta Giuliana. It has been restored and now serves as the municipality's cultural centre.
new.tip: Walk the short vaulted passage and check the exhibition space inside; the gate is quietest in the morning.
new.q: Famagusta Gate (Pyli Ammochostou), Nicosia

new.title: Step into the Selimiye Mosque, a Gothic cathedral
new.desc: Begun in the early 13th century as the Lusignan Cathedral of Saint Sophia and consecrated in 1326, it became a mosque after the Ottoman conquest of 1570, when two minarets were added. It is the main Gothic landmark of North Nicosia.
new.tip: Remove shoes and cover shoulders and knees; avoid prayer times, especially Friday midday.
new.q: Selimiye Camii (Ayasofya Katedrali), Selimiye Meydanı, Lefkoşa

new.title: Explore the Ottoman caravanserai Büyük Han
new.desc: Built in 1572 soon after the Ottoman conquest, the Great Inn is the largest and best-preserved caravanserai on Cyprus. It served as a prison under the British and was restored in the 1990s; it now holds craft shops, galleries and cafés around its courtyard.
new.tip: Visit in the morning before tour groups arrive and climb to the upper gallery for views over the courtyard.
new.q: Büyük Han, Asmaaltı Sokak, Lefkoşa

new.title: Look over the divided city from Shacolas Tower
new.desc: The 11th-floor observatory of the Shacolas Tower on Ledra Street gives a panorama of Nicosia, with boards tracing the Green Line that has split the capital since 1974. A small museum accompanies the viewing platform.
new.tip: Go on a clear afternoon; the telescopes make it easy to spot the Selimiye minarets and the Kyrenia range.
new.q: Shacolas Tower Museum and Observatory, Ledra Street, Nicosia

new.title: See Cyprus's richest Byzantine icons
new.desc: The Archbishop Makarios III Cultural Foundation museum, in the grounds of the Archbishop's Palace, holds one of the island's most important collections of Byzantine art, with icons and frescoes from the 9th to 19th centuries.
new.tip: Look into neighbouring Agios Ioannis Cathedral with its frescoes; check opening days before going.
new.q: Byzantine Museum, Archbishop Kyprianos Square, Nicosia

new.title: Tour the Hadjigeorgakis Kornesios Mansion
new.desc: This 18th-century Ottoman-era mansion belonged to Hadjigeorgakis Kornesios, the Greek Cypriot dragoman who held power at the turn of the 19th century. It now serves as an ethnological museum with carved wooden ceilings and a traditional courtyard.
new.tip: Allow about 45 minutes; the upper rooms are the best preserved.
new.q: Hadjigeorgakis Kornesios Mansion, Patriarchou Grigoriou 20, Nicosia

new.title: Visit the Byzantine church of Chrysaliniotissa
new.desc: Built in 1450 by Queen Helena Palaiologina, Panagia Chrysaliniotissa ('Our Lady of the Golden Flax') is regarded as the oldest Byzantine church in Nicosia. It sits in a restored quarter beside the Green Line and the Famagusta Gate.
new.tip: No longer used for regular services but often open for exhibitions; the surrounding streets are good for a walk.
new.q: Panagia Chrysaliniotissa, Chrysaliniotissa quarter, Nicosia

new.title: Meet the dervishes at the Mevlevi Tekke Museum
new.desc: The former Mevlevi lodge beside the Kyrenia Gate dates from the late 16th century and houses the tombs of 16 sheikhs of the order, with exhibits on dervish life and the whirling ceremony.
new.tip: Ask about occasional sema performances; modest dress is expected.
new.q: Mevlevi Tekke Müzesi, Girne Caddesi, İbrahimpaşa, Lefkoşa

new.title: Peek into the Dervish Pasha Mansion
new.desc: This 18th-century mansion in the Arabahmet quarter was bought by the Turkish Cypriot state in 1981 and opened as an ethnographic museum in 1988. Its rooms show Ottoman-era domestic life.
new.tip: Pair it with a walk through the old houses of the Arabahmet quarter.
new.q: Derviş Paşa Konağı, Mehmet Akif Caddesi, Arabahmet, Lefkoşa

new.title: Trace Nicosia's history at the Leventis Museum
new.desc: The Leventis Municipal Museum, founded by the Anastasios G. Leventis Foundation with the Nicosia Municipality and inaugurated in 1989, tells the city's story from the Chalcolithic period to the present through reconstructed interiors.
new.tip: Check the museum site for current hours; entry has been free in recent years.
new.q: Leventis Municipal Museum, Ippokratous 15-17, Nicosia

new.title: Steam in the Hamam Omerye
new.desc: This bath beside Tyllirias Square, dated by the Nicosia municipality to around 1570-71, was restored in 2002-2004 and works as a traditional Turkish bath today. Some sources link its site to an earlier Augustinian church.
new.tip: Book ahead and bring a swimsuit.
new.q: Hamam Omerye, Tyllirias Square, Nicosia

new.title: Take a bath in the medieval Büyük Hamam
new.desc: The Great Bath near İplik Pazarı, dated to 1309 on Wikipedia, is the only original Turkish bath still operating in North Cyprus. It keeps the classic sequence of changing room, warm room and a domed hot room with a central massage platform.
new.tip: Go in the afternoon and ask for the traditional scrub and foam massage.
new.q: Büyük Hamam, Çeşme Sokak, İplik Pazarı, Lefkoşa

new.title: Walk across the Ledra Street border crossing
new.desc: The pedestrian checkpoint on Ledra Street, open since 2008, links the Republic of Cyprus side with North Nicosia in a couple of minutes on foot, past the buffer-zone barricades and straight into the old town on the other side.
new.tip: Carry your passport; the crossing is open daily and queues are usually short.
new.q: Ledra Street Crossing, Nicosia

new.title: Eat a no-menu meze feast at Zanettos
new.desc: This old-town taverna, open since 1938, sends out a rotating spread of Cypriot meze such as pork belly, sheftalia, calf liver and halloumi, finishing with traditional sweets. There is no food menu.
new.tip: Book in the evening and arrive hungry; the portions are generous.
new.q: Zanettos Taverna, Trikoupi 65, Nicosia

new.title: Explore Kyrenia Castle and its ancient shipwreck
new.desc: The Byzantine-Crusader fortress above the old harbour was rebuilt by the Venetians in the 16th century. Its lower halls house the Shipwreck Museum with a 4th-century BC Greek merchant ship found off Kyrenia, with its cargo of amphorae.
new.tip: Allow two hours and go before midday; the harbour view from the ramparts is best in late light.
new.q: Girne Kalesi (Kyrenia Castle), Kordonboyu, Girne

new.title: Wander the Gothic ruins of Bellapais Abbey
new.desc: Founded by Augustinian canons in the early 13th century under the Lusignans, the abbey's Gothic cloister and refectory are among the finest on Cyprus. Lawrence Durrell lived in the village and wrote Bitter Lemons here.
new.tip: Visit early or late for the best light.
new.q: Bellapais Manastırı (Bellapais Abbey), Beylerbeyi, Girne

new.title: Climb to the fairy-tale St Hilarion Castle
new.desc: Perched on a ridge of the Kyrenia range, St Hilarion commands the pass between Kyrenia and Nicosia and is the best preserved of the three mountain castles.
new.tip: Go early in summer as there is little shade; wear sturdy shoes for the steps to the upper keep.
new.q: Saint Hilarion Castle (Aziz Hilarion Kalesi), Dikmen, Girne

new.title: Hike up to Buffavento Castle
new.desc: The 'Defier of the Winds', about 960 m above sea level, sits between St Hilarion and Kantara and was used to pass signals along the range. Its views span both coasts.
new.tip: The final climb is steep; carry water and go in the morning.
new.q: Buffavento Kalesi (Buffavento Castle), Girne

new.title: Walk the ancient city of Soli
new.desc: Near Lefke, Soli was one of the ancient city-kingdoms of Cyprus, with a Roman theatre and a basilica holding a swan mosaic.
new.tip: Combine with nearby Vouni Palace; bring water as there is little shade.
new.q: Soli Antik Kenti (Soli Ancient City), Gemikonağı, Lefke

new.title: Climb to the Persian-era Vouni Palace
new.desc: The ruins of Vouni Palace stand on a hilltop about 250 m above the sea near Lefke, reportedly destroyed by fire around 380 BC. Finds from Vouni are displayed in the Güzelyurt museum.
new.tip: The road up is narrow and winding; the sea view from the terraces is the reward.
new.q: Vouni Sarayı (Vouni Palace), Gemikonağı, Lefke

new.title: See Vouni and Soli finds at the Güzelyurt museum
new.desc: The Güzelyurt Archaeology and Nature Museum, in the old Omorfo metropolitan building next to the church of St Mamas, displays finds from Vouni Palace and ancient Soli.
new.tip: Open in the daytime with an early closing; combine with the orange groves around Morphou.
new.q: Güzelyurt Arkeoloji ve Doğa Müzesi, Güzelyurt (Morphou)

new.title: Stroll through the stone lanes of Karmi
new.desc: Karmi (Karaman), set at about 350 m in the hills west of Kyrenia, is known for whitewashed cottages, stone villas and bougainvillea. Its Greek Cypriot inhabitants left in 1974, and expatriates have since settled there.
new.tip: Walk the narrow lanes in the morning and stop at a village pub or restaurant.
new.q: Karmi (Karaman) Köyü, Girne

new.title: Order the Full Kebab at Niazi's
new.desc: A long-running family restaurant on Kyrenia's waterfront, said by Fodor's to have served its 'Full Kebab' since 1949 alongside meze, şeftali kebab and lamb chops.
new.tip: Share the Full Kebab; service is relaxed so allow time.
new.q: Niazi's Restaurant, 20 Temmuz Kordonboyu Caddesi, Girne

new.title: Linger over coffee at the Tree of Idleness
new.desc: The shady terrace opposite Bellapais Abbey claims the 200-year-old robinia tied to Lawrence Durrell's Bitter Lemons, with views of the abbey and the coast. It serves Cypriot lunches and coffee.
new.tip: Come outside peak lunchtime; a drink under the tree is enough.
new.q: Huzur Ağacı (Tree of Idleness), Bellapais, Beylerbeyi, Girne

new.title: Watch for nesting turtles at Alagadi Beach
new.desc: Alagadı, about 19 km east of Kyrenia, is a protected nesting beach for green and loggerhead turtles monitored by the SPOT conservation group, with hatchlings emerging from mid-July to September.
new.tip: The beach is closed at night in the season (8pm to 8am); the SPOT centre gives guided information.
new.q: Alagadı Kaplumbağa Plajı (Alagadi Turtle Beach), Girne

new.title: Walk the ramparts of Othello Castle
new.desc: Famagusta's harbour citadel is a Lusignan fortress remodelled by the Venetians, its name drawn from Shakespeare's Othello. Columns taken from Salamis stand in the courtyard.
new.tip: Go in the morning; the battlements give views over the old port.
new.q: Othello Kalesi (Othello Castle), Gazimağusa

new.title: See the Gothic Lala Mustafa Pasha Mosque
new.desc: Built from about 1298 to 1326 as the Cathedral of Saint Nicholas, this Lusignan Gothic landmark became the Lala Mustafa Pasha Mosque in 1571, named after the Ottoman commander of the siege. Its twin towers are said to echo Reims Cathedral.
new.tip: Cover up and remove shoes; avoid prayer times.
new.q: Lala Mustafa Paşa Camii (Saint Nicholas Cathedral), Gazimağusa

new.title: Explore the ruins of ancient Salamis
new.desc: The ancient city-state north of Famagusta preserves a colonnaded gymnasium, baths, a theatre and an agora, with the Bronze Age Royal Tombs between the ruins and Enkomi.
new.tip: Allow two hours; bring water as shade is scarce.
new.q: Salamis Antik Kenti (Ancient Salamis), Tuzla, Gazimağusa

new.title: Visit the Monastery of St Barnabas
new.desc: The monastery opposite the Salamis turnoff houses an icon museum and an archaeological collection with finds from Salamis and Bronze Age Enkomi, and commemorates the apostle Barnabas.
new.tip: Combine with Salamis the same morning.
new.q: Aziz Barnabas Manastırı (St Barnabas Monastery), Tuzla, Gazimağusa

new.title: See the mosaic floors of the Agia Trias basilica
new.desc: The ruins of an early Christian basilica from the late 5th or early 6th century stand in an olive grove at the edge of Sipahi village, with an intricately patterned mosaic floor.
new.tip: Stop here on the drive along the Karpaz coast road.
new.q: Agia Trias Bazilikası, Sipahi, İskele

new.title: Climb Kantara Castle for the Karpaz view
new.desc: The easternmost of the three Kyrenia range castles guards the entrance to the Karpaz peninsula and was refortified under King James I. From its ramparts the coast and Kaplica are visible.
new.tip: Combine with the Karpaz drive; the climb is short but steep.
new.q: Kantara Kalesi (Kantara Castle), Kantara, Gazimağusa

new.title: Reach the Apostolos Andreas Monastery
new.desc: At the north-eastern tip of the island stands the pilgrimage monastery of Apostolos Andreas, visited by Greek and Turkish Cypriots alike. The last stretch of the road is rough and the monastery has been under restoration.
new.tip: Allow half a day from Dipkarpaz; check the road condition and restoration status.
new.q: Apostolos Andreas Manastırı, Zafer Burnu, Dipkarpaz

new.title: Taste dondurma and baklava at Petek
new.desc: The Famagusta branch of Petek, a family bakery in business since the late 1970s, is known for cakes, lokum, baklava and ice cream that Lonely Planet rates among the best on the island.
new.tip: Try the dondurma after the old town; breakfast is also served.
new.q: Petek Pastanesi, Liman Yolu Sokak, Gazimağusa

new.title: Order a set kebab meal at Aspava
new.desc: A Famagusta Turkish restaurant on Liman Yolu Sokak, praised by reviewers for its set kebab meals and its view over the bay.
new.tip: Go for the set kebab meal; weekend lunch is busy.
new.q: Aspava Restaurant & Bar, Liman Yolu Sokak, Gazimağusa

new.title: Swim at Golden Beach on the Karpaz
new.desc: Golden Beach (Nangomi) is a long stretch of pale sand and clear water near the tip of the Karpaz peninsula, widely considered the best beach in the north.
new.tip: Bring water and food, as there are almost no facilities; go early in the day.
new.q: Altın Plaj (Golden Beach), Dipkarpaz, İskele

new.title: Walk through the ghost town of Varosha
new.desc: Varosha (Maraş), Famagusta's abandoned resort quarter, has been partly open to visitors since October 2020 along a marked route, with decaying hotels and beachfront.
new.tip: Stay on the marked route: no entering buildings and no drones.
new.q: Maraş (Varosha), Gazimağusa

new.title: Explore the Bronze Age city of Enkomi
new.desc: Enkomi is a 2nd-millennium BC settlement near Famagusta, a copper-trading centre that some scholars identify with the Alashiya of the Amarna Letters. Excavations, notably by Claude Schaeffer, found rich tombs and the Ingot God and Horned God bronzes.
new.tip: Little shade and few signs, so bring water. Most of the finds are in the Cyprus Museum in south Nicosia.
new.q: Enkomi Antik Kenti (Enkomi archaeological site), Tuzla, Gazimağusa

new.title: Find the frescoes of Antiphonitis church
new.desc: Antiphonitis is a 12th-century domed church built over a spring in the Kyrenia mountains, near the village of Kalograia (Bahceli). A 15th-century narthex was added, and its frescoes are among the finest on the island.
new.tip: Open roughly 08:30 to 17:00 in summer, but sometimes locked even in those hours, so go early. Combine with Kantara or Bellapais.
new.q: Antifonitis Kilisesi (Antiphonitis Church), Bahçeli (Kalograia), Girne

new.title: Trace Cypriot history at the Cyprus Museum
new.desc: Founded in 1882 under British rule, the Cyprus Museum is the island's oldest and largest archaeological museum, with the biggest collection of Cypriot antiquities anywhere. Its galleries run from the Neolithic to the Roman period and include many finds from Enkomi and Salamis.
new.tip: Allow at least two hours and check opening days before going.
new.q: Cyprus Museum, 1 Museum Street, Nicosia

new.title: Step into the Armenian Church of Notre Dame de Tyre
new.desc: Founded in 1116 as a Benedictine abbey church and rebuilt after the 1303 earthquake, this Gothic church passed to the Armenian Church in the late 15th century. A restoration finished in 2013 and won a Europa Nostra award in 2015.
new.tip: It stands in the Arab Ahmet quarter just north of the Green Line; ask at the entrance if it is open that day.
new.q: Ermeni Kilisesi (Notre Dame de Tyre), Salahi Şevket Sokak, Arabahmet, Lefkoşa

new.title: Visit the Kyrenia Gate in the old walls
new.desc: Built by the Venetians in 1567 and restored by the Ottomans in 1821, this is the northern gate of Nicosia's walls. Its upper guardhouse level was added in Ottoman times, and today it holds a tourist information office.
new.tip: A good starting point for exploring north Nicosia on foot; the gate itself is free to see.
new.q: Girne Kapısı (Kyrenia Gate), Girne Caddesi, Lefkoşa

new.title: See Zaha Hadid's Eleftheria Square
new.desc: Eleftheria Square, where Ledra and Onasagorou streets meet, was redesigned by Zaha Hadid and Christos Passas after a 2005 competition. The project was held up by archaeological finds and opened in stages in 2021, reconnecting the old town with the Venetian moat.
new.tip: Best in the evening when the old-town cafes around it fill up.
new.q: Eleftheria Square (Plateia Eleftherias), Nicosia

new.title: Wander the Nestorian Church in Famagusta's old town
new.desc: The Church of St George the Exiler, usually called the Nestorian Church, dates from the 14th century and was built for the Church of the East. Under the Ottomans it served as a camel stable, and today it hosts cultural events run by Eastern Mediterranean University.
new.tip: Often locked; the exterior and the surrounding Gothic ruins are worth the short walk from Othello Castle.
new.q: Nesturi Kilisesi (Nestorian Church), Gazimağusa Surlariçi

new.title: Grab a hot cheese pie at Hurricane bakery
new.desc: This family bakery at the foot of Ledra Street has hardly changed since opening in 1942. Its cheese pies, now made with a blend of cheeses, come out hot in the morning, alongside almond croissants and tahini rolls.
new.tip: Go in the morning for the first batch; take-away is cheaper than sitting.
new.q: Hurricane Confectionery, Nikokleous, Nicosia

new.title: Order şeftali kebab at Çember
new.desc: Çember is a Lefkoşa grill restaurant known for şeftali kebabı, the Cypriot minced-meat kebab wrapped in caul fat, as well as et şiş and Cypriot-style köfte. It sits beside the state hospital on Dr Burhan Nalbantoğlu Avenue.
new.tip: Open daily from 09:00 to 23:00; arrive early at weekends.
new.q: Çember Restaurant, Dr. Burhan Nalbantoğlu Caddesi, Lefkoşa

new.title: Dine on sardines behind Kyrenia Castle
new.desc: Hürdeniz Balık serves fish to order at tables behind one of the Venetian castle's towers, beside the sea. Reviewers praise the Cypriot sardines and octopus, though some find it pricey.
new.tip: Ask prices before ordering fish by weight.
new.q: Hürdeniz Balık Restorant, behind Kyrenia Castle, harbour, Girne

new.title: Try fish pastırma at Grida Balık in Çatalköy
new.desc: A small husband-and-wife fish restaurant in Çatalköy, praised for BBQ sea bass and fish soup, and for fish pastırma and calamari.
new.tip: Small place, so book at weekends.
new.q: Grida Balık Restaurant, Hazreti Ömer Caddesi 20/1, Çatalköy, Girne

new.title: Have sea bass at Silver Rocks in Lapta
new.desc: A seaside restaurant on the Lapta coast with views over the water and mountains, known for sea bass and fillet steak.
new.tip: Open daily from mid-morning to midnight; sunset is the best time.
new.q: Silver Rocks Restaurant, Fevzi Çakmak Caddesi, Lapta, Girne

new.title: Climb the keep of Kolossi Castle
new.desc: Kolossi Castle is a Gothic keep completed in 1454 by the Knights of St John, on the site of an earlier 13th-century Crusader fortress. The surrounding estate ran large sugar mills, and the commandery gave its name to Commandaria, the sweet wine.
new.tip: Opens daily with a small entry fee; go early before tour buses. Kourion is 10 minutes' drive away.
new.q: Kolossi Castle, Kolossi, Limassol

new.title: Watch the sunset from the Kourion theatre
new.desc: Kourion was a powerful city-kingdom on a cliff above Episkopi Bay, with most visible remains from the Roman and early Byzantine periods. The restored Greco-Roman theatre still hosts summer performances, and mosaic floors survive in the House of Eustolios.
new.tip: Bring a hat; there is little shade. Evening light over the bay is best.
new.q: Kourion Archaeological Site, Episkopi, Limassol

new.title: Explore Limassol Castle and its medieval museum
new.desc: Limassol Castle in the old town was rebuilt by the Ottomans around 1590 over a Byzantine and Lusignan fortress, and tradition says Richard the Lionheart married Berengaria of Navarre here in 1191. It houses the Cyprus Medieval Museum with armour, ceramics and tombstones.
new.tip: Allow about an hour; the roof gives views over the old port.
new.q: Limassol Castle (Cyprus Medieval Museum), Irinis Street, Old Town, Limassol

new.title: Visit the Holy Cross Monastery in Omodos square
new.desc: The monastery of Timios Stavros stands in the cobbled square of Omodos and is said to keep a fragment of the True Cross. Its icons and carved woodwork are matched by a museum of local lace and wine-making.
new.tip: Wander the surrounding lanes afterwards for zivania and Commandaria tasting.
new.q: Timios Stavros Monastery, Plateia Omodou, Omodos, Limassol

new.title: See the gilded interior of Kykkos Monastery
new.desc: Kykkos, founded in the late 11th century and dedicated to the Virgin Mary, is the richest monastery in Cyprus. Its courtyard is covered in mosaics and murals, and the museum shows icons and church treasures; Archbishop Makarios III began his career here as a novice.
new.tip: Dress modestly. Makarios's tomb is a short drive away at Throni.
new.q: Kykkos Monastery, Marathasa, Nicosia district

new.title: Find the 12th-century frescoes of Panagia Phorviotissa at Asinou
new.desc: Founded in 1105/6, this small stone church with a steep timber roof is covered inside with frescoes from the 12th to 17th centuries. It is one of ten Troodos painted churches on the UNESCO list.
new.tip: Ask at the Nikitari village coffee shop if the church is locked; check opening times first.
new.q: Panagia Phorbiotissa (Asinou Church), Asinou, Nikitari, Nicosia district

new.title: Admire the Byzantine murals of Panagia tou Araka
new.desc: This 12th-century church at Lagoudera has some of the finest late-Comnenian wall paintings in the Byzantine world, including a celebrated Pantocrator in the dome. It is on the UNESCO list.
new.tip: Photography inside is permitted; ask the keeper nearby for the key.
new.q: Panagia tou Araka, Lagoudera, Nicosia district

new.title: Step inside St Nicholas of the Roof near Kakopetria
new.desc: Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis is a UNESCO-listed church from the 11th century whose high pitched timber roof shelters Byzantine frescoes from the 11th to 17th centuries. It stands in the valley below Kakopetria's old quarter.
new.tip: Combine with a walk through Kakopetria's preserved old village.
new.q: Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis, Kakopetria, Nicosia district

new.title: Wander the rock-cut Tombs of the Kings
new.desc: This necropolis north of Paphos harbour dates from the 3rd century BC and was used by Ptolemaic officials and aristocrats, not kings. Chambers are cut into the bedrock, some with Doric columns and frescoed walls.
new.tip: Go in the late afternoon for softer light and fewer visitors.
new.q: Tombs of the Kings, Leoforos Tafon ton Vasileon, Kato Paphos

new.title: Follow the Roman mosaics of the House of Dionysos
new.desc: The Paphos Archaeological Park covers much of the ancient Greek and Roman city of Nea Paphos and is a UNESCO site. The House of Dionysos, the largest villa, has about 556 square metres of mosaics showing Dionysos and Greek myths, seen from raised walkways.
new.tip: Allow two hours and bring water; shade is limited.
new.q: Paphos Archaeological Park, Kato Paphos

new.title: Climb Paphos Castle at the harbour
new.desc: This small fort at the end of the harbour mole was rebuilt by the Lusignans in the 13th century, restored by the Ottomans and later used as a prison and salt store. Restoration was completed in 2015, and the roof gives views over the harbour.
new.tip: Entry is a few euros; it also hosts summer performances.
new.q: Paphos Castle, Harbour, Kato Paphos

new.title: Stop at Aphrodite's Rock, Petra tou Romiou
new.desc: This sea stack beside the Paphos-Limassol road is where myth says Aphrodite rose from the sea foam. Local tradition also ties the name to the Byzantine hero Digenes Akritas, and the pebble beach is a popular swimming spot.
new.tip: The sea can be rough and climbing the rock is not allowed; use the underpass to reach the beach.
new.q: Petra tou Romiou, Kouklia, Paphos district

new.title: Enter St Neophytos's cave hermitage near Tala
new.desc: The Enkleistra was carved into a cliff by the recluse Neophytos in the 12th century and painted in 1183, with frescoes among the best of the period. Nearby stand the monastery church and a museum of 16th-century icons.
new.tip: The ticket covers monastery and hermitage; closed on a few major holidays.
new.q: Agios Neophytos Monastery (Enkleistra), Tala, Paphos

new.title: See the carved iconostasis of Agios Lazaros
new.desc: The church in central Larnaca was built over the reputed second tomb of Lazarus, found in 890. Its baroque gilded iconostasis was restored in the 1970s, and a procession takes place on Lazarus Saturday.
new.tip: Dress modestly; the crypt with the tomb is below the altar.
new.q: Agios Lazaros Church, Plateia Agiou Lazarou, Larnaca

new.title: Visit Hala Sultan Tekke beside the Salt Lake
new.desc: This mosque and tekke on the west shore of Larnaca Salt Lake is the chief Muslim shrine in Cyprus, built around the tomb of Umm Haram, a companion of the Prophet. The present complex dates from 1813 and sits among palms.
new.tip: Remove shoes and cover shoulders and knees; entry is free.
new.q: Hala Sultan Tekke, Larnaca Salt Lake, Larnaca

new.title: Walk under the arches of the Kamares Aqueduct
new.desc: The Kamares (Bekir Pasha) Aqueduct was built by the Ottomans in the 1740s to bring water from the Tremithos river to Larnaca, and its stone arches still stand beside the road into town.
new.tip: Best at golden hour; it is a quick stop on the way to Hala Sultan Tekke.
new.q: Kamares Aqueduct, Larnaca

new.title: Trace Phoenician Kition at the Bamboula excavations
new.desc: Ancient Kition was a city-kingdom with Mycenaean and Phoenician temples from the 13th to 9th centuries BC, and the birthplace of the philosopher Zeno. Excavation areas lie scattered through modern Larnaca.
new.tip: Combine with the nearby Larnaca district museum.
new.q: Kition Archaeological Site, Archiepiskopou Kyprianou, Larnaca

new.title: Step into the round houses of Choirokoitia
new.desc: This Neolithic settlement on a hillside, occupied from about the 7th millennium BC, is a UNESCO site. Reconstructed round houses show how people farmed and buried their dead under the floors.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes; the slope is steep. Allow 1.5 hours.
new.q: Choirokoitia Archaeological Site, Choirokoitia, Larnaca district

new.title: Climb to Stavrovouni, the Mountain of the Cross
new.desc: This monastery sits on a rocky summit above the highway, one of the oldest in Cyprus. Women are not admitted inside, but the views over the plain are broad.
new.tip: Open only certain hours; dress modestly and check beforehand.
new.q: Stavrovouni Monastery, Stavrovouni, Larnaca district

new.title: Browse the Pierides Museum in an old Larnaca house
new.desc: Cyprus's oldest private museum holds around 2,500 pieces from Bronze Age terracotta to Roman and Byzantine art, in a colonial-era house in the town centre.
new.tip: Allow an hour; ideal for a hot or wet afternoon.
new.q: Pierides Museum, Zenonos Kitieos, Larnaca

new.title: Learn about Lefkaritika lace in a Pano Lefkara house
new.desc: The Museum of Traditional Embroidery and Silversmith-work occupies the late-19th-century House of Patsalos. Lefkara lace is on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list (2009), known for hemstitch and satin-stitch patterns.
new.tip: Entry is cheap; buy lace only from makers who show hand-worked pieces.
new.q: Local Museum of Traditional Embroidery and Silversmith-work (House of Patsalos), Pano Lefkara

new.title: See the Venetian-era monastery at Ayia Napa's centre
new.desc: The monastery in the town centre, built around a cave where an icon of the Virgin was said to have been found, has a Venetian fountain and a quiet courtyard. It gave the town its name.
new.tip: Free to enter; quiet in the morning before the square wakes up.
new.q: Ayia Napa Monastery, Plateia Seferi, Ayia Napa

new.title: Taste Cypriot wine at the Cyprus Wine Museum in Erimi
new.desc: The museum traces Cypriot winemaking from antiquity through ancient jars, medieval drinking vessels and old documents, with tasting available. It sits in Erimi, between Limassol and Kourion.
new.tip: Check current hours before going.
new.q: Cyprus Wine Museum, Pafou Street, Erimi, Limassol

new.title: Taste village wines at Oenou Yi winery near Omodos
new.desc: Oenou Yi is a family estate near Omodos making wines from indigenous grapes and Commandaria. Visits include a tasting among the vineyards of the Krasochoria.
new.tip: Book ahead for visits.
new.q: Oenou Yi Winery, Omodos, Limassol district

new.title: Hike to Caledonia Waterfall from Platres
new.desc: A 3 km nature trail follows the Krios Potamos river through pines and ferns to the 12 m Caledonia Waterfall at about 1,330 m, the best known in Cyprus. The loop takes under an hour from Pano Platres.
new.tip: Wear shoes with grip; stepping stones can be slippery after rain.
new.q: Caledonia Waterfalls, Caledonia Trail, Psilo Dendro, Pano Platres

new.title: Walk the Aphrodite Nature Trail from the Baths of Aphrodite
new.desc: A circular 7.5 km walk starts at the Baths of Aphrodite on the edge of the Akamas peninsula, climbs past an old oak and the Queen's Tower ruins and returns with views over Chrysochou Bay.
new.tip: Carry water; start early in summer.
new.q: Baths of Aphrodite, Akamas, Neo Chorio, Paphos district

new.title: Sail from Latchi harbour to the Blue Lagoon
new.desc: Boats leave the fishing harbour of Latchi for the turquoise Blue Lagoon on the Akamas coast, with snorkelling stops on the three-to-four-hour trips.
new.tip: Book morning departures; bring reef shoes.
new.q: Latchi Harbour, Latchi, Polis Chrysochous, Paphos district

new.title: Visit the Lara Bay turtle conservation station
new.desc: The station protects nests of green and loggerhead turtles on Lara beach, an isolated beach on the Akamas coast. Nesting runs from May to August, and visits are free.
new.tip: The track is rough; a 4x4 suits it best. There are no facilities, so bring water.
new.q: Lara Bay Turtle Conservation Station, Lara Beach, Pegeia, Paphos district

new.title: Dive the MS Zenobia wreck off Larnaca
new.desc: The Swedish ferry Zenobia capsized in 1980 on her maiden voyage and lies about 1.5 km offshore at 16-42 m with over 100 trucks in the hold, often rated among the world's top wreck dives. Non-divers can take glass-bottom boats from the marina.
new.tip: Operators require recent dive experience; boats depart from Larnaca marina.
new.q: Larnaca Marina, Larnaca

new.title: Watch flamingos on Larnaca Salt Lake
new.desc: Between about November and March thousands of flamingos feed on brine shrimp at this complex of four salt lakes, once a major salt-export source. Wading out to the birds is forbidden.
new.tip: Bring binoculars and keep to the shore.
new.q: Larnaca Salt Lake, Larnaca

new.title: Walk the sea cliffs and caves of Cape Greco
new.desc: The 385 ha national forest park on the cape east of Ayia Napa has marked paths along cliffs above sea caves, a picnic site, a bike path and snorkelling coves.
new.tip: Cliff jumping is at your own risk; bring water, as there is little shade.
new.q: Cape Greco National Forest Park, viewpoint, Ayia Napa

new.title: Swim at Fig Tree Bay in Protaras
new.desc: Fig Tree Bay is a calm, clear-water beach in Protaras named for a lone fig tree at its edge, with loungers for hire.
new.tip: Arrive early in summer; it fills up.
new.q: Fig Tree Bay, Protaras, Paralimni

new.title: Eat a Cypriot meze at Karatello Tavern
new.desc: Karatello is an old-town tavern serving traditional meze and local wines, praised in a 2025 Cyprus Mail review.
new.tip: Order the full meze for sharing; book at weekends.
new.q: Karatello Tavern, Old Town, Limassol

new.title: Dine by the fireplace at Lofou Tavern
new.desc: Lofou Tavern (Agrovino) serves Cypriot dishes in a stone building in the hill village of Lofou, with an open fire in winter.
new.tip: Stay for Commandaria and a village walk.
new.q: Lofou Tavern, Lofou, Limassol district

new.title: Have a homestyle lunch at Laona in Paphos
new.desc: A family-run Cypriot restaurant down an old-town passage on Votsi Street, mostly a lunch spot with main courses around ten euros.
new.tip: Book for dinner.
new.q: Laona Restaurant, Votsi Street, Paphos

new.title: Order the EUR 22 meze at Agora Taverna
new.desc: A Paphos taverna with good-value Cypriot meze in a lively spot, reviewed by the Cyprus Mail in 2023.
new.tip: Go hungry for the mixed meze.
new.q: Agora Tavern, Talat Pasa 1, Paphos

new.title: Eat casseroles at Mosfilos Tavern in Polis
new.desc: A tavern in a listed stone building serving traditional casseroles, legumes and oven dishes with local produce for about 17 years.
new.tip: Sit under the vine on the summer terrace.
new.q: Mosfilos Tavern, 23 Arsinois Street, Polis Chrysochous

new.title: Order the fish meze at To Arxontikon on Finikoudes
new.desc: A seafront restaurant on the Finikoudes promenade known for its fish meze of around 20 dishes at a modest price.
new.tip: Share between two or more.
new.q: To Arxontikon, Athenon 24, Finikoudes, Larnaca

new.title: Eat hearty Cypriot soul food at Militzis
new.desc: A local favourite tavern in Larnaca where residents gather for traditional Cypriot cooking.
new.tip: Go early for lunch.
new.q: Militzis Restaurant, Piale Pasa 42, Larnaca

new.title: Try a traditional Cypriot meal at Stou Roushia
new.desc: A tucked-away restaurant in downtown Larnaca, a short stroll from Finikoudes, praised by the Cyprus Mail in 2026 for traditional food.
new.tip: Book a table ahead.
new.q: Stou Roushia, Larnaca

new.title: Eat grilled mountain trout at Psilo Dendro in Platres
new.desc: Psilo Dendro serves trout from its own fish farm at Platres, grilled simply and eaten beside the stream.
new.tip: It closes in the early evening, so go for lunch.
new.q: Psilo Dendro Restaurant, Pano Platres, Limassol district

new.title: Order mushrooms and grills at Ais Giorkis in Kakopetria
new.desc: A popular village tavern in Kakopetria known for grilled dishes, meze and seasonal mushrooms.
new.tip: Reserve at weekends.
new.q: Ais Giorkis (Ais Giwrkis), Agiou Georgiou, Kakopetria

new.title: Eat souvla at Two Flowers in Pedoulas
new.desc: A Pedoulas restaurant praised for its owner's cooking and its souvla, charcoal-roasted meat on a long skewer.
new.tip: Stop after visiting Kykkos or the Pedoulas church.
new.q: Two Flowers Restaurant, Pedoulas, Nicosia district

new.title: Meet a pygmy hippo at Ayia Napa's Thalassa Museum
new.desc: Thalassa Municipal Museum of the Sea opened in 2005 and tells the story of Cyprus and the sea from prehistory onwards. Its highlights include a complete skeleton of an extinct pygmy hippopotamus over 75,000 years old, a clay sarcophagus from the Makronissos tombs and a basement marine-life collection.
new.tip: Allow about an hour; entry costs a few euros and it is a good rainy-day stop. The museum is a short walk from the harbour.
new.q: Thalassa Museum of the Sea, Kryou Nerou 14, Ayia Napa

new.title: Wander the Ayia Napa Sculpture Park above the sea
new.desc: An open-air park of about 20,000 square metres opened by the municipality in 2014 on the rocky slope towards Cape Greco. It displays works left by the annual Ayia Napa International Sculpture Symposium, arranged among rocks and pines that fall away to the sea.
new.tip: Entry is free and the park is open year-round. Go in late afternoon when the light on the stone is softer and it is cooler.
new.q: Ayia Napa Sculpture Park, Cape Greco Avenue, Ayia Napa

new.title: Climb down into the rock-cut Makronissos tombs
new.desc: A Hellenistic and Roman necropolis of 19 rock-cut tombs, a small sanctuary and part of an ancient quarry, excavated by the Ayia Napa municipality in 1989-90. Most tombs have a stepped entrance leading to a chamber with burial benches.
new.tip: Free to enter and open daily; bring a torch for the darker chambers. It sits close to Makronissos beach, so combine it with a swim.
new.q: Makronissos Tombs, Makronissos Avenue, Ayia Napa

new.title: Explore the acropolis of ancient Amathus
new.desc: Amathus was one of the ancient city-kingdoms of Cyprus, with an important sanctuary of Aphrodite said to rank second only to Paphos. The site east of Limassol holds the agora, harbour remains, a temple on the hilltop acropolis and early Christian basilica ruins.
new.tip: Visit in the morning or late afternoon, as there is little shade on the hill. Check opening hours with the Department of Antiquities.
new.q: Amathus Archaeological Site, Amathountos Avenue, Agios Tychonas, Limassol

new.title: Trace the cult of Aphrodite at Palaepaphos in Kouklia
new.desc: Palaepaphos was the great sanctuary of Aphrodite Paphia, a pilgrimage centre for centuries and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980. The Kouklia museum is housed in a Lusignan-era manor within the site and displays the sacred conical stone found at the altar.
new.tip: Combine the ruins with the museum, which is included in the ticket. It is about 14 km east of Paphos; go before midday in summer.
new.q: Palaepaphos Archaeological Site and Museum, Kouklia, Paphos

new.title: Browse the Limassol District Archaeological Museum
new.desc: The museum was founded in 1948 in part of Limassol Castle and has been in its current building near the Municipal Gardens since 1975. Three rooms show finds from the Limassol district from the Neolithic to the Roman period, with strong material from ancient Amathus.
new.tip: Entry is free according to local listings and the visit takes about an hour. Opening hours differ between sources, so check before going.
new.q: Archaeological Museum of Limassol, Anastasi Sioukri & Vyronos, Limassol

new.title: Walk the ramparts of Larnaca Castle and its Medieval Museum
new.desc: The fort stands at the southern end of the Finikoudes promenade, an Ottoman-era structure on older foundations. A three-room Medieval Museum inside shows Byzantine wall paintings, glazed pottery, Venetian helmets and swords, and Ottoman kitchen utensils.
new.tip: The roof terrace gives a view along the seafront. Check opening hours, as they differ by season.
new.q: Larnaca Medieval Castle, Leoforos Athinon, Larnaca

new.title: See the 6th-century apse mosaic at Panagia Angeloktisti, Kiti
new.desc: The Byzantine church in Kiti village was built over an early Christian basilica and keeps a 6th-century apse mosaic of the Virgin and Child between the archangels Michael and Gabriel on a gold ground. It is one of the best-preserved early Christian wall mosaics in Cyprus and is on the UNESCO Tentative List.
new.tip: The church can be locked outside visiting hours; check opening times first. Kiti is about 10 km south-west of Larnaca.
new.q: Panagia Angeloktisti Church, Kiti, Larnaca

new.title: Find the three-in-one painted churches of Agios Ioannis Lampadistis
new.desc: The monastery near Kalopanayiotis in the Marathasa valley combines the 11th-century church of Agios Ioannis, the chapel of Agios Irakleidios and a Latin chapel under a single timber roof. It is part of the UNESCO-listed painted churches of the Troodos.
new.tip: Frescoes span several centuries, so allow time for each chapel. Combine it with the sulphur-spring village of Kalopanayiotis just across the valley.
new.q: Monastery of Agios Ioannis Lampadistis, Kalopanagiotis, Nicosia district

new.title: Taste monastery wine at Chrysorrogiatissa
new.desc: Traditionally founded in 1152 by the monk Ignatios, the monastery above Pano Panagia has buildings mostly from 1770. Its old winery was reopened in the mid-1980s and sells its own wines, and the monastery is the site of a pilgrimage on 15 August.
new.tip: Dress modestly for the church and try the monastery wines at the winery shop. Pano Panagia, birthplace of Archbishop Makarios III, is nearby.
new.q: Chrysorrogiatissa Monastery, Pano Panagia, Paphos

new.title: See St Paul's Pillar beside Agia Kyriaki church
new.desc: The site in Kato Paphos holds the ruins of Chrysopolitissa, the largest early Byzantine basilica on the island, and the still-active Agia Kyriaki church. Tradition says St Paul was flogged at a pillar here before converting the Roman governor Sergius Paulus, although there are no written records to back that up.
new.tip: Entry to the archaeological site is free. It is a short walk from the harbour and the mosaics of the Archaeological Park.
new.q: Agia Kyriaki Chrysopolitissa and St Paul's Pillar, Kato Paphos

new.title: Tie a rag to the tree above the Agia Solomoni catacomb
new.desc: A Hellenistic chamber tomb turned Christian chapel in Kato Paphos, with five rock-cut compartments. Locals link it to the martyr Solomoni and the Seven Sleepers, and a terebinth above it is hung with rags left by pilgrims for healing; Crusader graffiti is cut into the plaster.
new.tip: It is small and quick to visit, right next to the Paphos Archaeological Park. The interior is dark, so bring a phone torch.
new.q: Agia Solomoni Catacomb, Apostolou Pavlou Avenue, Kato Paphos

new.title: Climb the 150-odd steps to Profitis Ilias chapel in Protaras
new.desc: A small whitewashed stone chapel on a granite hill above Protaras, reached by around 150 steps. It was rebuilt in the 1980s and is lit up at night; on a clear day the view extends along the coast towards Famagusta and the Karpas.
new.tip: Go at sunset for the light, but take water as there is no shade. Free to enter.
new.q: Profitis Ilias Chapel, Agiou Elia, Protaras, Paralimni

new.title: Step into the cave church at Ayia Thekla
new.desc: A whitewashed chapel on the cliffs west of Ayia Napa stands beside a cave church carved into the rock, said to have been a women's monastery until 1937. The beach below takes its name from the chapel and is quieter than the main Ayia Napa strands.
new.tip: The cave is open daily and free; bring a torch. The beach has a bar and restaurant nearby.
new.q: Ayia Thekla Chapel, Sotira, Famagusta district

new.title: Book a table for meze at Forsos Tavern in Mouttagiaka
new.desc: A long-standing tavern in a restored stone house with a green courtyard in Mouttagiaka, east of Limassol, known for a full meze of traditional Cypriot dishes. A Cyprus Mail review from December 2025 calls it a local institution, with meze at about 25 euros per head.
new.tip: Booking is essential. It is open evenings Monday to Saturday and closed on Sundays.
new.q: Forsos Tavern, Ayiou Eleftheriou 49, Mouttagiaka, Limassol

new.title: Order the fish meze at Karas Fish Tavern in Kapparis
new.desc: A family-run fish taverna on Kennedy Avenue in Kapparis, run by three brothers with the catch landed by the family boat. A 2023 Cyprus Mail review praised the fish meze and calamari alongside Cypriot dips, with the sea about 200 metres away.
new.tip: Fish meze was about 28 euros per person at review time. The tavern is a few minutes by car from Protaras.
new.q: Karas Fish Tavern, Kennedy Avenue 55, Kapparis, Protaras

new.title: Eat meze to live Greek music at the Old Village Tavern
new.desc: A stone-arched tavern on Nissi Avenue in Ayia Napa, fitted with antiques and serving homemade Cypriot meze, including a fish meze of nine seafood dishes. Live Greek music plays most evenings.
new.tip: Come in the evening for the music and book in high season. Order the traditional meze to share.
new.q: Old Village Tavern, Nissi Avenue 48, Ayia Napa

new.title: Share a massive meze at Kyra Giorgena in Larnaca
new.desc: A family taverna on William Weir Street run by the Konnaris family since 2000, serving a large traditional meze at around 20 euros per person according to a 2022 Cyprus Mail review. It has a garden in summer and live music on winter weekends.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday evenings (Sunday lunch too); closed Mondays. Arrive hungry.
new.q: Kyra Giorgena Tavern, William Weir 7, Larnaca

new.title: Sample Geroskipou loukoumi at Aphrodite Delights
new.desc: Geroskipou loukoumi, a Cypriot delight made without glucose or gelatine, holds EU protected geographical indication. The Aphrodite Delights shop opposite Geroskipou square has traded since 1895 and also sells almond dragees, pastelli and honey.
new.tip: Tasting before buying is normal. A second branch is on Kantarenas Street.
new.q: Aphrodite Delights, Archbishop Makarios III Avenue 57, Geroskipou, Paphos

new.title: Graze the Limassol Agora food hall in the 1918 market
new.desc: The municipal market by Saripolou Square, built in 1918 and popularly called Pantopolio, was renovated and reopened as a food hall in 2020-21. It combines stalls and small kitchens inside the original stone building.
new.tip: Open daily; food service stops earlier than closing time. A good wet-weather lunch spot in the old town.
new.q: Limassol Agora, Kanari 47, Saripolou Square, Limassol

new.title: Wade out to the islet at Nissi Beach
new.desc: A 500 metre Blue Flag beach in Ayia Napa named after the small scrub-covered islet about 60 metres offshore. In calm weather you can wade to the islet through shallow water.
new.tip: Go early for clearer water and fewer people. Wear water shoes for the rocks near the islet.
new.q: Nissi Beach, Ayia Napa

new.title: Swim in sheltered Konnos Bay among the pines
new.desc: A small Blue Flag beach of fine sand about 200 metres long, sheltered by steep pine-covered slopes on the Cape Greco road between Ayia Napa and Protaras. Lifeguards and sunbed hire operate in summer.
new.tip: Parking is limited in peak season; arrive before 10am. Buses 101 and 102 stop at the turn-off.
new.q: Konnos Bay, Cape Greco road, Protaras

new.title: Hike the narrow Avakas Gorge in the Akamas
new.desc: A limestone gorge in the Akamas with rock walls over 30 metres high, reached from a car park near Peyia. Short out-and-back routes suit most walkers, while loops lead on to the coast.
new.tip: Take water as there is none on the route. Wear sturdy shoes; the access track can be rough.
new.q: Avakas Gorge trailhead, Akamas, near Peyia, Paphos

new.title: Swim off Pissouri Bay's long Blue Flag beach
new.desc: A Blue Flag sand and shingle beach over a kilometre long beneath the village of Pissouri, known for multicoloured pebbles and clear water. The bay and village are separate communities, and the village keeps its Gothic-style church of Apostle Andreas from 1883.
new.tip: Combine with a walk up to the village for lunch. The beach is calmer in the morning.
new.q: Pissouri Bay Beach, Pissouri, Limassol

new.title: Walk the Artemis Trail around Mount Olympus
new.desc: A 7 km circular nature trail round the summit of Chionistra, the highest peak in Cyprus at about 1,850 metres. It is easy and mostly flat, through black pine forest, taking roughly 2.5 to 3 hours.
new.tip: No drinking water on the route and it is the coldest place on the island, so bring layers. It starts near Troodos Square.
new.q: Artemis Trail start, Troodos Square, Troodos

new.title: Taste wines at Vasilikon Winery in Kathikas
new.desc: A winery founded in 1993 in Kathikas on the Laona-Akamas wine route, with terraces over the vineyards, a wine museum and a restaurant. It is known for its Vasilikon and Ayios Onoufrios labels, made from native and international grapes.
new.tip: Book a tasting in advance; it is open in the daytime. The Akamas road continues from here.
new.q: Vasilikon Winery, Kathikas, Paphos

new.title: Taste Commandaria at Kyperounda Winery
new.desc: One of the highest wineries in Europe at around 1,140 metres, established in 1998 near Kyperounta in the Pitsilia hills. It makes the sweet Commandaria from Xynisteri and Mavro grapes and offers guided tastings.
new.tip: Weekday visits only according to one listing; reserve ahead. Pair with a drive through the Pitsilia villages.
new.q: Kyperounda Winery, Kyperounta, Limassol district
